# Rabe-ffi — Build & Usage Guide

C FFI binding for the [rabe](https://github.com/Fraunhofer-AISEC/rabe) (Attribute-Based Encryption in Rust) library, supporting CP-ABE and KP-ABE encryption/decryption for schemes like AC17, BSW, AW11, BDABE, MKE08, LSW, and YCT14.

Repo: https://github.com/Aya0wind/Rabe-ffi

## General Requirements

Regardless of Linux or Windows, the build process requires 3 components:

1. **Rust toolchain (nightly)** — mandatory, stable cannot be used (see [why](#why-rust-nightly-is-required)).
2. **`cargo-expand`** — the build script (`build.rs`) uses `cbindgen` with `with_parse_expand`. This tool is needed to macro-expand the code before generating the `.h` header.
3. **Linker + OS C build tools** (GCC/Clang on Linux/macOS, MSVC Build Tools on Windows).


## Build on Linux

### 1. Install Rust

```bash
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
source $HOME/.cargo/env
```

### 2. Install OS Build Tools

```bash
# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt update && sudo apt install build-essential

# Fedora / RHEL
sudo dnf groupinstall "Development Tools"

# Arch
sudo pacman -S base-devel
```

### 3. Set Nightly Toolchain + Install cargo-expand

```bash
rustup default nightly
cargo install cargo-expand
```

### 4. Clone and Build

```bash
git clone https://github.com/WanThinnn/librabe.git
cd Rabe-ffi
cargo build --release
```

### 5. Output

```
target/release/librabe_ffi.so     # dynamic library
target/release/librabe_ffi.a      # static library
rabe.h                             # header automatically generated by cbindgen (in project root)
```

### 6. Copy to Your Project

```bash
cp target/release/librabe_ffi.so /your/project/path
cp rabe.h /your/project/path/rabe.h
```

### 7. Compile & Link C/C++ Project on Linux

```bash
g++ your_app.cpp -I/your/project/path -L/your/project/path -lrabe_ffi -o your_app
```

Run (make sure the `.so` path is correct at runtime):

```bash
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/your/project/path ./your_app
```

Alternatively, copy `librabe_ffi.so` to `/usr/local/lib` and run `sudo ldconfig` so you don't have to set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` every time.



## Build on Windows (MSVC)

### 1. Install Visual Studio Build Tools (Required before installing Rust MSVC)

Download: https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/

In the installer, check:
- ✅ **Desktop development with C++**
  (includes MSVC v143 build tools + Windows 10/11 SDK)

### 2. Install Rust — via PowerShell or CMD (DO NOT use MSYS2/Git Bash)

> ⚠️ If you run the installer from MSYS2/Git Bash, rustup might incorrectly select the `gnu` target instead of `msvc`. Always install from standard PowerShell or CMD.

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://win.rustup.rs/x86_64 -OutFile rustup-init.exe
.\rustup-init.exe
```

When prompted for installation options, select the default (Enter) — on standard PowerShell/CMD, rustup correctly identifies `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` as the default host triple.

**If you previously installed rustup with the `gnu` target**, fix it with:

```powershell
rustup target add x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
rustup toolchain install nightly-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
rustup default nightly-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
```

Verify:

```powershell
rustup show
```

You should see:
```
Default host: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
active toolchain: nightly-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
```

### 3. Install cargo-expand

```powershell
cargo install cargo-expand
```

### 4. Clone and Build

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/WanThinnn/librabe.git
cd Rabe-ffi
cargo build --release
```

### 5. Output

```
target\release\rabe_ffi.dll         # dynamic library
target\release\rabe_ffi.dll.lib     # import lib (used to link against the .dll)
target\release\rabe_ffi.lib         # static library
rabe.h                               # header
```

### 6. Integrate into Visual Studio Project

1. Copy `rabe_ffi.dll`, `rabe_ffi.dll.lib`, and `rabe.h` to your project.
2. Project Properties → **VC++ Directories**:
   - Include Directories: add the path containing `rabe.h`
   - Library Directories: add the path containing `rabe_ffi.dll.lib`
3. Project Properties → **Linker → Input → Additional Dependencies**: add `rabe_ffi.dll.lib`
4. Copy `rabe_ffi.dll` into the same directory as the output `.exe` (or add it to PATH) so it can be loaded at runtime.

If you want to static-link (no need to distribute the `.dll`), use `rabe_ffi.lib` instead of `rabe_ffi.dll.lib` in Additional Dependencies.

---

## Build on Windows (MinGW) — Optional

Only use this if your entire C++ project (including other libraries like CryptoPP) is already built with MinGW/g++, to avoid mixing two different runtimes.

```powershell
rustup toolchain install nightly-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu
rustup default nightly-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu
cargo install cargo-expand

git clone https://github.com/WanThinnn/librabe.git
cd Rabe-ffi
cargo build --release
```

If the linker (`gcc.exe`/`ld.exe`) is not found, install it:

```powershell
winget install --id=BrechtSanders.WinLibs.POSIX.UCRT -e
```
(or use MSYS2: `pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-gcc`), then add it to your PATH.

Output:
```
target\release\rabe_ffi.dll
target\release\librabe_ffi.dll.a   # import lib (MinGW format)
target\release\librabe_ffi.a       # static lib
```

Link with g++:
```bash
g++ your_app.cpp -L./target/release -lrabe_ffi -I. -o your_app.exe
```

> **Performance Note**: MinGW and MSVC both use the LLVM backend for code generation in Rust, so execution speed (especially for heavy pairing/AES computations) is nearly identical. The only differences are in linking/exception handling mechanisms, which do not affect ABE performance.

---

## Integration into C/C++ Projects

Minimal example using `rabe.h`:

```c
#include "rabe.h"

int main() {
    Ac17SetupResult keys = rabe_ac17_init();
    // ... use keys.public_key, keys.master_key ...
    
    rabe_ac17_free_public_key(keys.public_key);
    rabe_ac17_free_master_key(keys.master_key);
    return 0;
}
```

See more complete examples in the unit tests (`#[cfg(test)] mod test`) within the `src/cp_abe/` and `src/kp_abe/` files in the Rabe-ffi source code.



## Why Rust Nightly is Required

The project's `build.rs` uses `cbindgen` with this configuration:

```rust
cbindgen::Builder::new()
    .with_parse_expand(&["rabe-ffi"])
    ...
```

`with_parse_expand` requires macro-expanding the entire crate before generating the header (because the code uses macros like `to_json_impl!`, `from_json_impl!`, and `free_impl!` to generate C export functions — `cbindgen` cannot read the macro contents natively). This expansion requires `cargo-expand`, which depends on `-Z unpretty`, a feature only available in **nightly rustc**.



## Security Notes

- **Dependencies**: The project currently uses `rabe = "0.4.x"`. Starting from `rabe 0.3.1`, it utilizes `aes-gcm` (an AEAD scheme with an authentication tag) for the internal symmetric encryption layer, which is cryptographically sound. Previous versions used unauthenticated AES.
- **Memory Safety**: Severe undefined behavior bugs (like incorrect memory layouts when freeing pointers with `Box::from_raw` instead of `CString::from_raw`, and borrowing C pointers via `String::from_raw_parts`) have been patched out of this FFI wrapper.
- **Audits**: There are no official RUSTSEC advisories for `rabe`/`rabe-bn` at the time of writing. However, keep in mind this is an academic cryptography library and has not yet undergone an independent security audit. It is highly recommended to run `cargo audit` periodically and assess the risks before using it for sensitive production data.
